page: Vultr vhp-2c-4gb-amd is a cloud compute instance in the High Performance family, configured with 2 shared vCPUs derived from a single physical core across two hardware threads. The processor is an AMD EPYC x86_64 CPU clocked at 2.0 GHz, supported by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. Memory is provisioned at 4.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Local persistence is supplied via a 100 GB NVMe SSD, and each instance includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address without dedicated GPU hardware accelerators.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate modest computational throughput constrained by the shared two-thread core setup. Single-core stress-ng CPU performance registers within the average tier at 2263.16, while multi-core stress-ng tests fall into the lower quartile at 4483.12. Geekbench testing yields scores of 1116.0 for single-core execution and 2013.0 for multi-core throughput, alongside low scores in clang software compilation and ray tracing. Memory bandwidth tests record 20.06 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 20.37 GB/sec for writes. In application benchmarks, the instance achieves 1.85 million Redis SET operations per second and 1.3 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Hardware instruction flags include AVX, FMA, BMI2, AES, and SHA_NI, whereas AVX-512 extensions and AMX units are absent. As a shared-thread entry-tier configuration with integrated NVMe storage, this instance offers a cost-effective operational profile for lightweight services. However, the shared core topology and constrained 4.0 GB memory footprint make it ill-suited for intensive parallel computation, heavy compilation tasks, or large-scale in-memory databases. Appropriate deployments include small microservices, lightweight web servers, basic background worker scripts, and non-critical staging or development environments.
description: Vultr vhp-2c-4gb-amd is a High Performance tier virtual server delivering 2 shared vCPUs and 4.0 GB of system memory, underpinned by an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz. The allocation represents two threads sharing a single physical core, coupled with 16 MB of L3 cache and supported by hardware-level AES and SHA_NI acceleration. Storage is provided through a 100 GB NVMe SSD alongside a complimentary public IPv4 address, with no discrete GPU accelerators. Benchmarks place multi-core compute throughput in lower performance tiers, reflected by a Geekbench multi-core mark of 2013.0 and static web serving throughput of 1.3 GB/sec. Uncached memory read bandwidth tests measure approximately 20.06 GB/sec. The configuration serves as an economical resource profile designed for entry-level workloads, including lightweight web serving, small container hosting, development environments, and low-concurrency background services where dense computational resources are unnecessary.
